To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the use of MRI for breast cancer detection in women with a genetic predispostion has resulted in a significant increase of the number of biopsies, but also in an increase of breast cancer detection and a decrease of interval cancer.

the introduction of MRI-guided vacuum-assisted biopsy of the breast is feasible, that the technique is safe and effective, that it is possible to obtain a sufficient number of tissue samples with this new technique, that the procedure can be carried out with minimal discomfort to the patient and that it is a good alternative to surgical biopsy.
the use of MRI in patients at familial risk for breast cancer may lead to overdiagnosis and that the psychological impact of MRI in this group of patients may be underestimated.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of MRI-guided biopsy of breast lesions.
the development of new biopsy techniques, which can be used under MRI guidance.

the following issues: (i) the development of a new MRI-compatible breast biopsy system; (ii) the development of MRI-compatible vacuum-assisted biopsy instruments; (iii) the use of MRI-guided vacuum-assisted biopsy for the detection of nonpalpable breast cancer; (iv) the use of vacuum-assisted biopsy in the detection of non-palpable breast lesions; and (v) the development of an MRI-compatible breast biopsy needle guide.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the introduction of MRI-guided biopsy of breast lesions is not only technically feasible, but also necessary in order to avoid unnecessary surgery and to improve patient care in the future.

MRI of the breast is not a panacea for the early detection of breast cancer.

the introduction of MRI in the diagnostic work-up of patients with breast cancer and in screening programmes for high-risk patients will lead to a considerable increase in the number of biopsies performed and to the detection of a larger number of breast cancers, but also to an increased number of unnecessary biopsies.
